kandidater.fil: File:Carrière du Wingertsberg - éruption du Laacher See.jpeg
kandidater.beskrivning: La couche supérieure, soit l'ULST - Upper Laacher See Tephra - est la zone la plus riche en phénocristaux et en minéraux mafiques. La couche moyenne - MLST, Middle Laacher See Tephra - présente des échantillons plus hétérogènes et de couleur variable. Dans le bas, les ponces blanches éjectées en premieres - LLST , Lower Laacher See Tephra - forment des strates horizontales, chaque strate correspondant à une explosion. Elles sont fortement vacuolaires et contiennent peu de phénocristaux.

handelser.plats: Nevalı Çori vid Eufrat, Şanlıurfaprovinsen, Turkiet (i dag under vatten)

kandidater.fil: File:Urfa museum Nevalı Çori Temple in 2025 1225.jpg
kandidater.beskrivning: A Turkish text has, translated "The temple, also called the Obelisk Building, is the only structure with a square plan among the 29 structures unearthed in the excavations and is 14x14 meters in size. This temple is significantly different from all other structures unearthed in the Neolithic layers of the Nevali Çori settlement in terms of location, plan, size and interior arrangement. In the Southeastern Anatolia Region, the construction of cult structures outside the residential area has become a general trend since the beginning of the b phase of the Pre-Pottery Neolithic Age. It is understood that the building had two construction phases. The second phase is the renewal of the structure in the first layer of the first phase and it is understood that some construction elements were reused. There is a platform made of large flat stones along the inner side of the walls surrounding the temple. There are 12 stones erected on the platform at certain intervals. There are two more obelisks in the middle part. The height of this obelisk was measured as 2.35 meters. There are two human arm reliefs continuing downwards with a certain slope on both wide sides. These also bend to the r face and form hands. Accordingly, it is thought that these obelisks are stylized human statues like those at Göbeklitepe. It is understood that more care and effort was spent in the construction of the base, walls and obelisks than would be expected in a residential building."

kandidater.beskrivning: Neolithic polished stone axehead fragment. From towards the butt end, but both ends broken and large flake broken off one surface (ancient damage). Longitudinal striations on middle of both surfaces, and diagonal striations at the edges/sides - presumably from polishing. Patinated brown-grey all over, except for tiny chip revealing blue-grey stone - probably Great Langdale stone. Length 52.1mm, width 39mm-50.5mm, thickness 22.4mm, weight
kategorier: Neolithic artefacts in the Portable Antiquities Scheme

kandidater.fil: File:Neolithic Great Langdale Polished Stone Axehead (FindID 192567).jpg
kandidater.kredit: https://finds.org.uk/database/ajax/download/id/149491 Catalog: https://finds.org.uk/database/images/image/id/149491/recordtype/artefacts archive copy at the Wayback Machine Artefact: https://finds.org.uk/database/artefacts/record/id/192567
kandidater.beskrivning: An incomplete Neolithic polished stone axehead. The green coloured axe is sub-triangular in plan and pointed oval in cross section. The axe tapers in thickness to the cutting edge, which is still very sharp. The tip of the butt end is missing and there are some small chips removed on both faces. The greenstone comes from Great Langdale in Cumbria. The surviving length is 97.7mm, the width at the cutting edge is 61.2mm, the thickness is 26.5mm and the weight is 220.0g.
kategorier: Neolithic artefacts in the Portable Antiquities Scheme

kandidater.kredit: https://finds.org.uk/database/ajax/download/id/553352 Catalog: https://finds.org.uk/database/images/image/id/553352/recordtype/artefacts archive copy at the Wayback Machine Artefact: https://finds.org.uk/database/artefacts/record/id/767612
kandidater.beskrivning: A damaged and incomplete stone axe of Neolithic date, probably a Group VI Langdale axe. The stone axe has been polished and is grey-green in colour. The axe is made from a fine-grained siliceous tuff, a sedimentary volcanic rock which was orignally deposited in water and is likely to be from the Great Langdale quarries in Cumbria. The axe is damaged, missing most of one side and some of the blade edge on both surfaces. The break may have occured during use, as it appears to originate from the blade end (Alison Roberts pers. comm ). c. 4000-2351 BC.
